newsitem.title: USA: Fluor reports loss, abandons growth target.
newsitem.headline: Fluor reports loss, abandons growth target.

text.p: Fluor Corp. reported a loss for its second fiscal quarter Wednesday and said it was no longer prudent for the construction and engineering company to pursue its goal of achieving 20 percent earnings growth this year.
Chief Executive Officer Les McGraw said the company instead will focus on improving its profits.
McGraw's statements followed the release of disappointing second quarter results for Fluor and its principal subsidiary, the construction and engineering company Fluor Daniel.
Fluor posted a net loss of $70.1 million, or 83 cents a share, in the second quarter ended April 30, and has lost $8.1 million for the year to date.
In last year's second quarter, it had a profit of $63.7 million, or 75 cents a share.
Revenues rose to $3.18 billion from $2.58 billion.
The company said it expects Fluor Daniel to turn in an operating profit of $140 million in the second half of fiscal 1997. Fluor Daniel reported an operating loss of $36 million in the first half.
Fluor Daniel said the company's $100 million cost reduction programme should be completed by year end.

McGraw said Fluor's A.T. Massey Coal unit is poised to benefit from greater deregulation of the electric utility industry and from more stringent environmental standards. Fluor stock closed up $1.125 at $52 on the New York Stock Exchange.
